subject: Site telemetry: request for tracker inventory and DPIA scope
messages:
From: J. Sullivan <jsullivan@acme-consumer.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: PixelWatch Integration <integration@pixelwatch.com>, PrivacyOps <privacy@acme-consumer.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tracker inventory + DPIA scope for upcoming audit

Hi Olga,

Hope you’re well. We’re preparing for a vendor privacy audit tied to GDPR obligations and need a concise mapping of all site telemetry for our July–Aug 2025 traffic window. Specifically: a) a list of first- and third-party trackers/pixels (domain, provider, purpose, data categories), b) whether the tracker reads/writes identifiers (cookie/localStorage/KV), c) which legal basis we recommend for each (consent/legitimate interest), and d) an initial DPIA scope for any trackers that profile or process special categories.

Can Redwood provide the inventory and a short DPIA scoping note by next Tuesday (Aug 19)? Also helpful: any existing CAIQ/SIG evidence that speaks to site telemetry controls (cookie governance, CMP integrations, data minimization). We can share the audit template if helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that’s easier.

-j
J. Sullivan
Privacy Lead, Acme Consumer Health
privacy@acme-consumer.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: J. Sullivan <jsullivan@acme-consumer.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tracker inventory + DPIA scope for upcoming audit

Hi J.,

Thanks for the heads up — we can take this on. Quick clarifying q’s before we scope:
- Do you want data sampling limited to public pages (marketing) or also product pages that require login?
- Is the DPIA required to address profiling for personalization or also analytics-only flows?
- Any required recipients for the CAIQ/SIG evidence (e.g., do you need redacted SOC 2 artifacts)?

I’ll pull internal folks together (legal + security + product) and get an inventory to you by Aug 19 if the scope is marketing + public pages. If you need product-area telemetry included, I’ll need until Aug 21.

Also looping in our privacy lead Naomi and Dev (infra) to help gather artifacts.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Partnerships & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tracker inventory + DPIA scope for upcoming audit

Thanks Olga — quick guidance from legal:
- For public marketing pages we can operate under the consent basis where the CMP is present; for cross-site advertising pixels we should assume individual consent is required unless the pixel is strictly anonymized.
- DPIA: scope to include any trackers that perform profiling (ad personalization, predictive scoring) or transfer data outside the EEA/UK.
- CAIQ/SIG: we can share the standard SIG Lite that covers data flow and encryption; for SOC 2 we must provide redacted reports via secure link only (we’ll coordinate with Security).

Dev — can you run the tag scan and provide a CSV of detected tags + network endpoints + cookie flags? Try to include when the tag fires (page types) and whether it uses local IDs.

Marissa — please prepare the DPIA draft language for trackers that profile and a short mitigation matrix (consent flow, opt-out, data retention).

Naomi
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Aug 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tracker inventory + DPIA scope for upcoming audit

Folks — attached is the first-pass export from our runtime-based tag scanner for public pages (sample window: 2025-07-01 to 2025-08-01). CSV includes: domain / provider / script URL / firing page examples / cookie names / storage type / first-party vs third-party / observed identifiers column.

High-level notes:
- PixelWatch (pw-track.js) is used across marketing pages for attribution and sets a persistent id cookie (pw_id).
- Google Analytics (gtag.js) is active via consent and is set to IP anonymize on EU pages; it does not set special category profiling but does capture page-level behavior.
- A small ad partner (adwise.io) is present on two campaign landing pages and appears to set cross-site identifiers.
- Several third-party widgets (chat, feedback) use localStorage for session tokens but do not appear to send user profile data to external advertising networks.

I attached site-telemetry-inventory.csv and a short dump of network endpoints. I’ll follow up if we need product-area scans.

Dev
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: site-telemetry-inventory.csv (text/csv)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: J. Sullivan <jsullivan@acme-consumer.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, PixelWatch Integration <integration@pixelwatch.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tracker inventory + DPIA scope for upcoming audit

Hi J.,

Thanks for your patience — please find the initial artifacts attached and scope recommendations below. Attachments: site-telemetry-inventory.csv; dpi-assessment-draft.pdf; cookie-governance-notes.docx. Link to redacted SIG/CAIQ and SOC 2 access is at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_site-telemetry (we’ll share secure links per your process).

Summary of what we delivered:
- Inventory (CSV) with observed tags, domains, firing contexts, and whether an identifier is set.
- DPIA draft that flags PixelWatch and Adwise as in-scope for profiling; proposed mitigations include: explicit consent gating via CMP for personalization flows, limiting retention for cross-site IDs to 30 days, server-side aggregation for analytics where possible, and blocking third-party ad calls on EU pages where consent absent.
- Cookie governance notes with recommended update to our privacy policy (cookie section) to explicitly list partners and retention windows.

Next steps we propose:
1) Review the CSV and DPIA draft and indicate whether you want product pages included (if yes, we’ll run a broader scan and update the DPIA).
2) Confirm if you need the full SOC 2 artifact (we will provide a secure, redacted copy under an NDA).
3) Optional call: Wed Aug 20 at 14:00 UTC to walk through findings and the mitigation matrix — I’ve tentatively held that slot.

If that timeline works, we’ll finalize the DPIA language and provide the CAIQ/SIG export.

Best,
Olga
Director, Partnerships & Compliance
Redwood Inference
